svg.text: C Standalone sub-mechanisms (1 of 2) — vessel tricks for any concept
Each panel loops on its own. None of these needs a moving part inside the food.
source: C-universal-vessel.md section 5
S-1, S-2, S-19 in C-stack · S-4, S-6 in C-sandwich · S-10, S-16 in C-skin
S-3 Freeze-plate lid for wet slices
A Peltier plate at −10 °C freezes the surface film in 1–2 s,
lifts one slice off the stack, lays it flat and lets go on a
reversed current pulse. No hole, no crevice.
S-5 Breading by flipping

g.text: cutlet + loose coating fall together into the next vessel

svg.text: Flour, egg and crumb vessels: the next one is clamped upside down
on top and the pair is turned over. No gripper touches the wet
cutlet. About 8 flips of 5 s.
S-7 Form in the cooking vessel

g.text: fried where they lie, flipped as a set

svg.text: Do not make a patty and move it: press the mass flat in the pan,
part it into 4 (GN 1/3) or 8 pieces of 110 g, fry in place,
clamshell-flip the whole set.
S-8 Glass-cutter egg opening

g.text: silicone cups on two coaxial spindles

svg.text: One turn against a scoring wheel, then the cups pull apart: the
shell breaks along the score like cut glass, yolk whole, half
shells stay on the cups for the bin.
S-9 Freeze to count

g.text: tray turned over and everted: pucks pop out
a paste is now a counted piece

svg.text: Tomato paste, butter, stock, herbs are frozen once in a silicone
tray of 5 g and 20 g cells. No pump, no tube, no residue;
accuracy = cell size (±2.5 g).
S-11 Orifice and vibrated sieve as valves
Nothing moves in the food path. One orifice collar and one sieve
collar dose all dry goods.
